Subject: Post-call: Tool-calling integration patterns & SDK/auth follow-ups

Hi Samir / Aisha — thanks again for the time today. Good discussion; capturing the key technical takeaways and proposed next steps so we’re aligned. I copied Michael and Dylan for the technical follow-up.

TL;DR: Redwood can support the tool-calling patterns you described (parallel external calls + structured output), recommended approach below. Next step: 30-min technical deep-dive with Dylan to validate latency/SLOs and auth.

What we learned
- Use case: customer support automation + transactional workflows. LLM orchestrates external systems: bank lookup, invoice fetch, and a payments tool. Latency target: ~800ms P50 for common queries, <2s P90 for fan-out flows.
- Current infra: FinApps runs services in us-west-2; wants private routing and ability to pin to a dedicated model for predictable latency once in production.

Recommended integration patterns (high level)
1) SDK setup & auth
   - Use Redwood SDK for streaming responses and function/tool calling. Quickstart attached (redwood-sdk-quickstart.md).
   - Auth: start with API-key for PoC, move to mutual TLS (mTLS) or customer-managed KMS for production (we support both).

2) Routing & model variants
   - Route interactive UI traffic to a lower-latency variant (smaller context / quantized) and heavy backend rerankers to a bigger model. We can configure policy-based routing (latency-first vs cost-first). See attached map (map-of-routing-policies.png).

3) Structured output & tool calling patterns
   - Tool definitions: define a compact JSON schema for each tool the model may invoke (name, inputs schema, timeout, retry policy).
   - Tool choice: prefer explicit tool invocation tokens in structured output (e.g., {"tool":"bank_lookup","args":{...}}) so tooling layer can deterministically route.
   - Parallel tools: Redwood supports issuing parallel tool calls from a single LLM response where the orchestrator fan-out is safe (idempotent reads). We recommend limiting to 3 parallel calls for P90 latency targets and using streaming to surface partial results.
   - Error handling: include a standard enum for tool errors (TEMPORARY, PERMANENT, RATE_LIMIT) and retry/backoff policies. For important reads, use hedged reads (issue in parallel across replicas) to reduce tail latency.

4) Embeddings & reranker
   - Use client-side embedding calls (we provide SDK helpers) + a lightweight FAISS/Elastic reranker. For scale, use dense-retrieval + a small neural reranker in Redwood for top-K re-scoring.

Proposed next steps
- Dylan to run a 30-minute deep-dive next week to validate end-to-end latency and auth options.
- I’ll share a mutual action plan (attached) and SDK quickstart.

Attachments: redwood-sdk-quickstart.md, map-of-routing-policies.png, mutual-action-plan-FinApps.pdf

Thanks — happy to iterate on the tool-definition examples below if you want.

Thanks Marissa — very helpful summary. A couple quick clarifications before we schedule the deep-dive:

2) Retry semantics: do you recommend the model request handle retries (i.e., return a "try again" instruction) or should the orchestration layer automatically retry specific tool calls? How do you surface transient tool errors back to the model so it can decide fallback behaviors?

3) Embeddings: curious about the reranker setup — is reranking inside the same Redwood request or a separate pipeline? Latency budget for support searches is tight.

Great questions — answers inline, plus a suggested plan for the deep-dive.

1) Parallel tool calls
   - Recommendation vs hard limit: the "3 parallel calls" is a conservative recommendation to meet the latency target; the runtime supports higher fan-out but tail latency grows non-linearly. For PoC we can support your 6-call flows, but we’ll want to measure P90 and consider batching or progressive disclosure if P90 is > 2s.

2) Retry semantics
   - Orchestration should own retries. Pattern: LLM emits structured tool call intent (tool + args + idempotency flag). Orchestrator calls the tool with per-tool retry/backoff and returns a structured result to the model (including error enum). The model then decides fallback (alternative tool, user prompt, or graceful degradation).
   - We’ll instrument transient errors with a TEMPORARY tag and include the original request id so the model can reason about retries.

3) Embeddings & reranker
   - Reranker can be run as part of the same Redwood flow (model-invoked reranker) or as a separate pipeline. For tight latency budgets we typically do a two-stage approach: embeddings nearest-neighbor (fast) -> local lightweight scorer -> optional full neural reranker for top-3. We’ll show latency tradeoffs in the deep-dive.

Example tool-definition (suggested canonical format)
{
  "name": "bank_lookup",
  "inputs": { "account_id": "string", "country": "string" },
  "timeout_ms": 500,
  "retry": { "policy": "exponential", "max_attempts": 2 },
  "idempotent": true
}

Error enum we ship: {"OK","TEMPORARY","PERMANENT","RATE_LIMIT","NOT_FOUND"}

Proposed technical deep-dive (30 min)

I attached a mutual action plan PDF and a quickstart doc to help your engineering team get running. Available slots next week: Tue 10-11am PT, Wed 2-3pm PT. Which works for you?

Marissa
